ad: Start: Aarey Milk Colony main gate, Goregaon East, Mumbai 400065
d: Quiet, green roads through Aarey Milk Colony with a steep climb - long-run and endurance territory for western-suburb runners, with almost no traffic in the early morning.
b: Distance runners, Hill training, Running groups

ad: Aksa Beach, Aksa Village, Malad West, Mumbai 400095
d: A roughly 3 km sandy beach lined with casuarina trees, one of the cleaner beaches in the city and a favourite for local morning walks and yoga. Do not swim - strong undertow, no lifeguards.
t: Best 6 AM – 7 PM (not recommended at night)

ad: Ambe Ghosale Talao, Thane West
d: Lake with a walking loop of about 650 m, close to Brahmala and Kachrali lakes — string them together for a longer run.

ad: Thane East
d: Thane East park with a walking and running loop of about 800 m.

ad: Gowalia Tank, Grant Road West, Mumbai
d: Historic Quit India maidan with a garden promenade used by walkers, plus playgrounds. A green loop in a dense neighbourhood.

ad: Fort, Mumbai
d: Historic cricket maidan in Fort with open space to walk or run around the edges of the pitches. Open round the clock.

ad: Bandra Reclamation, Bandra West, Mumbai
d: Promenade near the Bandra end of the Sea Link with a mix of paved and muddy paths — about 2 km of sea-view running.

ad: Bandstand Promenade, Byramji Jeejeebhoy Rd, Bandra West, Mumbai 400050
d: A 1.2 km BMC-run sea walkway with a jogging track along the rocks, ending at Bandra Fort and its amphitheatre. Good for running, jogging and walking; best early, before the sunset crowd.

ad: Mulund West, Mumbai
d: Neighbourhood garden in Mulund West with a short, flat walking loop (about 500 m).

ad: Bhakti Park, behind IMAX theatre, Wadala East, Mumbai 400037
d: A 25-acre park of grassland and wooded patches with over 4 km of jogging tracks and walking paths. Free and dog-friendly.

ad: Start: Bhayandar (West) Chowpatty
d: The creek-side chowpatty in Bhayandar West, maintained by MBMC. Open views over the water for a sunset walk or easy jog.

ad: Brahmala Talao, Thane West
d: Small neighbourhood lake with a walkable edge — a short flat loop (about 500 m) for laps.

ad: Start: Carter Road promenade (north end), Bandra West, Mumbai 400050
d: A flat, tree-lined 1.25-1.5 km seafront path, busy with runners, walkers and skateboarders, ending at Joggers Park. Extend it through Chuim village to the Bandstand promenade for about 3.7 km one-way. Busy, so go early.

ad: Swatantrya Sainik Udyan (Chimni Garden), Borla, Union Park, Chembur East, Mumbai 400071
d: A quieter garden next to the golf course with a walking track and outdoor gym equipment.

ad: Chintamani Garden, Mulund East, Mumbai 400081
d: A small Mulund East garden with a short, flat walking loop of about 0.2 miles.

ad: E Block, Bandra Kurla Complex, Bandra East, Mumbai
d: Landscaped park in BKC with paved pathways, gazebos and a giant chessboard. A calm loop for a lunchtime walk or easy run between office blocks.

n: Coastal Road Promenade (Breach Candy to Worli)
ad: Start: Priyadarshini Park end, Nepean Sea Road / Breach Candy, Mumbai 400026
d: The new sea-facing promenade along the Mumbai Coastal Road: about 5.25 km currently open from Priyadarshini Park past Haji Ali to Worli, with separate walking paths and a cycling track. Free, wide and uninterrupted - now one of the longest continuous seafront runs in the city.
t: Promenade open 24 hours; gardens along it 8 AM – 8 PM

ad: Near President Hotel, Colaba, Mumbai
d: 31,000 sq m urban woodland with a joggers' track under tall, old trees — rare shade for a South Mumbai run.

ad: Dadar Chowpatty, Dadar West, Mumbai 400028
d: A shoreline beach locals use for jogging and yoga, with a big view of the Bandra-Worli Sea Link at sunrise and sunset.

ad: Ghatkopar West, Mumbai
d: Ghatkopar West neighbourhood park with a short, flat walking loop of about 500 m.

ad: Erangal Gaon, Madh, Mumbai (just off Aksa Beach)
d: Quieter neighbour of Aksa Beach with dark, basalt-rich sand and one of the best sunsets on Madh Island. Good for a calm evening walk away from the Aksa crowds.

ad: Dr. Ashok Chopra Marg, Mangal Nagar, Versova, Andheri West, Mumbai
d: Large neighbourhood park with walking and jogging tracks, a football lawn and exercise equipment. No pets allowed.

ad: Diamond Garden, VN Purav Marg (Sion-Trombay Road), Chembur East, Mumbai 400071
d: Chembur's best-known garden, with jogging and walking tracks, an open-air gym and a retired Gnat fighter jet by the entrance.

ad: DK Sandu Udyan, next to Joy Hospital, Chembur East, Mumbai 400071
d: A neighbourhood garden with a walking track, gazebo and shaded seating - an easy morning walk loop.

ad: Start: Erangal village (lane through the village to the beach, by St Bonaventure Church), Erangal, Madh, Mumbai
d: Small, local village beach reached through the colourful lanes of Erangal on Madh Island. Quiet enough for an unhurried morning walk on the sand, with sea views from start to finish.
b: Walkers, Solo with a group, Families

ad: Five Gardens, Dadar Parsi Colony, Matunga, Mumbai 400014
d: Five small gardens in the old Parsi colony between King's Circle and Dadar, joined by tree-shaded residential roads. Easy to stitch together a flat 3-4 km loop.

ad: Hiranandani Gardens, Powai, Mumbai
d: Unmanicured, forest-style park in Hiranandani with a jogging track under tree cover — noticeably cooler than the streets around it.
t: 6 AM – 10 AM, then until 6 PM (per LBB)

ad: Gandhi Maidan, Plot No. 155, D. Saraswati Marg, Mahadeo Wadi, Chembur East, Mumbai 400071
d: An open ground that hosts local running groups and sports training, including YMCA programmes.

ad: Girgaon Chowpatty, Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Road, Girgaon, Mumbai 400007
d: The beach at the north end of Marine Drive, quiet in the early morning with locals walking, jogging and doing yoga on the sand. Easy to combine with a Marine Drive run.

n: Godrej Play Area & Jogging Track — Vikhroli East
ad: Opposite Godrej Platinum, Pirojshanagar 400079, Vikhroli, Mumbai
d: A play area with a jogging track opposite Godrej Platinum in Pirojshanagar, for an easy walk or run.

ad: Gorai Beach, Gorai village, Mumbai 400091
d: Peaceful, mostly empty beach at the far north-western tip of the city, with clean sand that suits a long relaxing walk and big sunsets. A few shacks sell snacks and you can rent a cycle there.

ad: Yari Road, Yagna Nagar, Versova, Andheri West, Mumbai
d: Small garden with a reflexology stone path alongside a regular cement walking loop, plus gym machines and yoga sessions.

n: Hanging Gardens and Kamala Nehru Park
ad: Hanging Gardens (Pherozeshah Mehta Gardens), Ridge Road, Malabar Hill, Mumbai 400006
d: Terraced gardens on top of Malabar Hill and the park opposite, popular with local morning walkers; an easy loop of about a mile with sea views.

ad: Start: Hatkesh, Mira Road (East)
d: A municipal jogging track laid along the Hatkesh nala in Mira Road East. A flat, traffic-free stretch for an easy early run.

ad: Hiranandani Gardens, Powai, Mumbai
d: Hiranandani park with a circular walking path around its periphery — easy laps away from traffic.

ad: Joggers Park, Hiranandani Estate, Thane West, Maharashtra 400607
d: Joggers park inside Hiranandani Estate, the meeting point for The Run Club Thane. A calm, traffic-free place for laps, with the estate roads around it for longer runs.

n: Jesal Park Chowpatty & Priyadarshini Joggers Park
ad: Start: Priyadarshini Joggers Park, Jesal Park Chowpatty, Bhayandar (East)
d: Bhayandar's creek-front promenade at Jesal Park, with a municipal joggers' park and gardens along the water. The go-to morning walk and run spot in Bhayandar East.

ad: Jewel of Navi Mumbai, Sector 26, Nerul, Navi Mumbai
d: Landscaped lakeside park in Sector 26 Nerul with an open-air gym and a Yulu bike zone; a calm spot for an evening jog or walk close to Palm Beach Road.

ad: Jijamata Udyaan, Lalbaug Flyover, near Byculla, Byculla East, Mumbai 400027
d: The city's old botanical garden and zoo, with well-shaded paths and flowering trees - a calm daytime walking loop in central Mumbai.

ad: Joggers Park, Carter Road (south end), Bandra West, Mumbai 400050
d: Seaside park at the south end of Carter Road with a 400 m loop: a mud strip for running plus two paved walking tracks. Opened in 1990 and still one of the city's busiest jogging spots.

ad: Juhu Beachfront Public Park, 15 Gandhigram Rd, Jukarwadi, Juhu, Mumbai 400049
d: A compact green park by Juhu beach with about 1 km of looped paths and tree-covered walkways - handy for a structured run before or after the sand.

ad: Creek Road, Lokhandwala Complex, Andheri West, Mumbai
d: Lokhandwala's joggers' park; LBB notes a free running club meeting here at 6 AM on Sundays, Tuesdays and Thursdays.

ad: Near Johnson & Johnson, LBS Road, Mulund West, Mumbai
d: One of Mulund's best-known gardens, with a jogging track open to the public.

ad: Bhandarwada Hill, behind Dockyard Road railway station, Mazgaon, Mumbai
d: A 1.5-acre BMC garden on a hilltop above a reservoir, with views over the harbour. Popular with joggers, senior walkers and students looking for a quiet corner.

ad: Start: Juhu Chowpatty, Juhu Tara Road, Juhu, Mumbai 400049
d: About 3 miles (around 5 km) of wide, flat sand from Juhu to Versova; firm underfoot at low tide and quiet in the early morning.

ad: Opposite Thane Municipal Corporation building, Thane West
d: City lake opposite the TMC headquarters with a central island and fountains; its edge makes an easy, flat loop of about 650 m.

ad: Kanti Nagar, Andheri East, Mumbai
d: Rectangular joggers' park with an inner running track and an outer walking track. Monthly pass system.

ad: Madh Marve Road, Madh, Mumbai (about 2 km from Madh jetty)
d: Quiet, low-key beach on the north-western edge of the city where locals come to jog and walk. Not fancy and not always clean on weekends, but good for a long, unhurried walk with Madh Fort and Madh Church close by.

ad: Madh Fort, near Kileshwar Mahadev Mandir, Kileshwar Road, Madh, Mumbai
d: Short walk and stair climb up to a 17th-century Portuguese fort at the southern tip of Madh Island, with views over the sea, Versova creek and the city skyline. Best timed for sunset.

ad: Mahalaxmi Race Course, Keshavrao Khadye Marg, Mahalaxmi, Mumbai
d: A 2.2 km dirt loop around the horse-racing track, opened to runners in the morning and evening. The soft surface is easier on the joints than the seafronts, which is why marathon trainees like it.

ad: Maharashtra Nature Park, Sion Bandra Link Road, opp. Dharavi Bus Depot, Dharavi, Mumbai 400017
d: A 37-acre man-made forest on the Mithi river, with shaded trails out to the Mahim creek mangroves. Go at opening for the birds and butterflies. There are no autos or cabs outside, so book a cab both ways rather than planning to walk on to BKC.

ad: Mahim Beach, Mahim Bay, near Mahim Fort / Mahim Koliwada, Mumbai 400016
d: A roughly 1 km beach on Mahim Bay with an emerging promenade, views across to Bandra and Worli, and early-morning joggers. Short and local rather than a long run.

ad: Elevated Nature Trail, Walkeshwar, Malabar Hill, Mumbai 400006
d: A raised wooden walkway through the treetops of Malabar Hill's forest, with views out over the city and sea. A slow walk rather than a run.

ad: Mango Garden, CBD Belapur, Navi Mumbai
d: Small neighbourhood garden in Belapur, good for a short walk or easy laps with kids.

ad: Koliwada, Manori, Mumbai (short walk from Manori jetty)
d: Wide, clean beach on Manori island, often called a mini Goa for its shacks, chapels and old East Indian homes. Great for long strolls and sunsets, and popular with weekend cyclists.

ad: Start: Marine Drive near Wilson College, Girgaon Chowpatty, Mumbai 400007
d: Mumbai's classic seafront run: about 4.3 km of flat promenade from Wilson College to Nariman Point, with the sea on one side and the skyline on the other. Well lit, so it works at night too, though it gets crowded even early.

ad: Marve Beach, near Marve jetty (Manori ferry), Malad West, Mumbai
d: Narrow beach at the northern end of Madh Island beside the Marve jetty, where ferries leave for Manori. Fine for a short walk with street-food stalls and fishing boats; most of the stretch is hemmed in by the INS Hamla naval base.

ad: Start: Masunda Lake (Talao Pali) next to Gadkari Rangayatan, Thane West
d: Central Thane's lake, about 15 minutes' walk from the station, with a promenade, food stalls and boating. Good for an early-morning loop before the crowds arrive.

ad: Millennium Garden, Ghatkopar East, Mumbai
d: A free, central Ghatkopar East garden with walking paths and benches.

ad: Mindspace Garden, MDP Road, Mindspace, Malad West, Mumbai 400064
d: A BMC-run garden in the Mindspace business district with over a hundred tree species, gazebos, a joggers' path and steps that double as a cardio workout. Free.

n: Nanalal D Mehta Garden (Matunga flyover park)
ad: Under Tulpule Flyover, near King's Circle station, Parsi Colony, Matunga, Mumbai
d: A 600 m mosaic-tiled walkway built under a flyover, lit at night. Narrow and central — good for a quick walk or easy laps.

ad: Start: lake entrance off Palm Beach Road, Nerul, Navi Mumbai
d: A dedicated 2.7 km path around Nerul Lake, also called Seawoods lake, just off Palm Beach Road. Traffic-free and pleasant for easy loops or a cool-down after the road run.

ad: Nirvana Park, Hiranandani Gardens, Powai, Mumbai 400076
d: A 4-acre landscaped park with a lit stone running track around lawns, a pond, gazebos and little bridges.

ad: Oval Maidan, between Maharishi Karve Road and the Bombay High Court, Fort, Mumbai 400032
d: A 22-acre heritage maidan with a jogging track around its edge, framed by Victorian Gothic and Art Deco buildings. No gates or fees; quieter on weekday mornings than on Sundays, when the cricket takes over.

ad: Start: Ahilya Gokul Patil Rd junction, Palm Beach Road, Nerul, Navi Mumbai
d: The 10 km six-lane road from Vashi to Belapur along the harbour is Navi Mumbai's favourite long run: smooth and well kept, with a footpath or shoulder for much of it. Go early, before the traffic builds.

ad: Linking Road, Khar West, Mumbai
d: Green pocket just off busy Linking Road with a jogging track nearly the size of Joggers Park and a softer mud path, plus a covered yoga area.

ad: Saki Vihar Road, IIT area, Powai, Mumbai
d: Lake-view walking park on Saki Vihar Road used for walking, jogging and casual football.

n: Powai Lake promenade and Hiranandani Garden
ad: Start: Hiranandani Garden, Hiranandani Gardens, Powai, Mumbai 400076
d: A 5.5 km mixed route: garden paths at Hiranandani, a 1.4 km lakeside promenade along Powai Lake, then wooded trails in Forest Park. Go early morning or late afternoon.

ad: Priyadarshini Park, Nepean Sea Road, Malabar Hill, Mumbai 400006
d: A sea-facing 20-acre park with a 400 m synthetic track and a 500 m coconut-lined dirt path - the place in South Mumbai for laps and intervals away from traffic.

ad: DN Nagar, Andheri West, Mumbai (next to DN Nagar metro station)
d: Renovated municipal garden with long, shaded, winding paths used by joggers and walkers, plus a free open-air gym.

ad: Start: Railadevi Lake, Road No. 4, Wagle Estate, Raheja Gardens, Thane West
d: A 20-acre lake in Wagle Estate, about 3 km from Thane station. Free to enter and fine for a short walk or jog around the edge.

ad: Rajawadi Garden, Ghatkopar East, Mumbai 400077
d: A small neighbourhood garden in Ghatkopar East with a short, flat walking loop of about 0.2 miles - fine for an easy morning walk close to home.

n: Rajiv Gandhi Joggers Park & Mini Seashore
ad: Rajiv Gandhi Joggers Park, Sector 10A, Juhu Nagar, Vashi, Navi Mumbai
d: One of the best running spots in Navi Mumbai: a flat 2.5 km path around a pond in a dedicated park, away from traffic. A bridge links it to the Vashi Mini Seashore (Juhu Chowpatty).

ad: Start: Late Rambhau Mhalgi Udyan, Ramdev Park, Mira Road (East)
d: One of MBMC's ten best-rated gardens, in Ramdev Park. A green neighbourhood spot for walking laps away from Mira Road's traffic.

ad: Rock Garden, Nerul, Navi Mumbai
d: One of Nerul's well-known gardens, a green stop for a short jog or walk.

ad: WG Union Road, Azad Nagar, Colaba, Mumbai
d: Twelve-acre Port Trust garden with a wide 650 m running track around the grounds — one of South Mumbai's best loops.

ad: Sagar Vihar, Sector 6, Vashi, Navi Mumbai
d: Waterfront promenade in Sector 6 Vashi that's popular with morning and evening joggers; a bridge connects it to the Mini Seashore. Hawkers can crowd it in the evenings.

n: Sambhaji Park (Sambhaji Raje Maidan), Mulund East
ad: Sambhaji Park Version II, Deendayal Nagar, Mulund East, Mumbai 400081
d: A big sports ground with a jogging track of almost 700 m, lit at night, plus an open gym and courts - Mulund East's go-to loop.

ad: Opposite Kanchan Junga Building, Sector 11, Koparkhairane, Navi Mumbai
d: A roughly 4 km path that sees few morning walkers, popular with dog owners — lots of room for an unhurried run.

ad: Sewri Jetty area, about 1 km from Sewri railway station, Sewri, Mumbai
d: Mangrove-lined mudflats on the harbour where thousands of migratory flamingos feed between roughly October and March. Go early on a winter morning for an easy walk and some of the best birdwatching in the city.

n: SGNP main gate to Kanheri Caves
ad: Sanjay Gandhi National Park main gate, Western Express Highway, Borivali East, Mumbai 400066
d: A 6 km one-way climb on the park road from the main gate to the Kanheri Caves through forest, with deer and birds along the way. Medium difficulty; park entry fees apply. Bicycles can be rented at the park to ride the same road.
b: Distance runners, Hill training, Nature lovers
t: Tue – Sun 7:30 AM – 6:30 PM (last entry 5 PM, closed Mon)

n: Shaheed Major Kaustubh Rane Joggers Park
ad: Start: behind Poonam Sagar Complex, Mira Road (East)
d: Municipal joggers' park behind Poonam Sagar Complex in Mira Road East. MBMC ranks it among the city's ten best gardens, and a handy spot for morning laps.

ad: Shivaji Park, Dadar West, Mumbai 400028 (pedestrian gate on the east side)
d: Mumbai's largest park (27 acres) with a flat 1.3 km perimeter path, the home ground of several running groups and marathon clubs. Easy to add laps or explore the interior paths.

ad: Road No. 1, Sion East, Mumbai
d: Garden at the base of 17th-century Sion Fort with walking paths, plus an easy hillock climb for views — good for hill repeats.
t: Morning till noon, 4 PM onwards (per LBB)

ad: Breach Candy, Mumbai
d: Sea-facing garden on Bhulabhai Desai Road with tree-lined paths, good for an evening walk; links up with the coastal promenade.

ad: Tilak Nagar, Kurla East, Mumbai
d: Municipal ground whose perimeter makes a flat loop of about 650 m — handy for laps in Tilak Nagar.

ad: Start: Upvan Lake, at the junction of Pokhran Road 1 and Pokhran Road 2, Thane West
d: One of Thane's biggest lakes, tucked against the Yeoor Hills and a favourite place for an easy evening run or walk. Lively and pretty during the Sanskruti arts festival.

ad: Start: Uttan beach, Uttan, about 8 km west of Bhayandar
d: The coastline at Uttan fishing village, on the western edge of Mira-Bhayandar. A quieter sand-and-sea alternative for a weekend morning walk or run.

ad: Keluskar Road South, Dadar West, Mumbai (near Shivaji Park)
d: Seaside garden near Shivaji Park with walking tracks and greenery, opening onto Dadar beach — a quieter alternative to the Shivaji Park loop.

ad: Veer Savarkar Udyan, Lokmanya Tilak Road, Gautam Nagar, Borivali West, Mumbai 400092
d: A seven-acre garden shaded by banyan and pipal trees, with a 1.5 km jogging track around its edge and a lake in the middle. About 10 minutes from Borivali station.

ad: Versova Beach, Versova, Andheri West, Mumbai 400061
d: A wide stretch of sand, less crowded than Juhu and much cleaner since the volunteer clean-up drives began in 2015 - good for a sunrise jog.

ad: Wonders Park, Sector 18, Nerul, Navi Mumbai
d: Big NMMC park in Sector 18 Nerul with replicas of the Seven Wonders, fountains and rides; paths suit easy jogs and family walks, and there's an NMMC open-air gym in the sector.

ad: Start: Worli Sea Face near Worli Post Office (Sea Link end), Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan Rd, Worli
d: A flat, roughly 2.75 km waterfront road with a 1.5 km separated path that starts just south of the Bandra-Worli Sea Link. Good for first-timers and interval work; go early, it gets windy and busy.

ad: Off Dr Ashok Chopra Marg, Versova, Andheri West, Mumbai
d: Green neighbourhood park with separate walking and running tracks, gym equipment and play areas. Mellow in the evenings.

ad: Start: Yeoor Hills gate, end of Pokhran Road 1, Thane West
d: The forest road climbing into Yeoor, the Thane side of Sanjay Gandhi National Park, is where Thane goes for its morning walk or run. Clean air and green all round, and the climb is good hill training.

n: Aarey Colony: Goregaon East to Powai
ad: Start: Aarey Milk Colony, Goregaon East, Mumbai 400065
d: A roughly 9.6 km ride on quiet, tree-lined Aarey roads from Goregaon East to Powai, past lakes, gardens and the Chhota Kashmir area. Easy-moderate (2/5).

ad: Carter Road promenade, Bandra West, Mumbai
d: Short cycling track along the Carter Road seafront, next to the promenade, dog park and chess tables.

ad: Start: Priyadarshini Park end, Breach Candy, Mumbai 400026
d: A dedicated cycling track along the new Coastal Road promenade, with ramps at the underpasses, running about 5.25 km from Breach Candy past Haji Ali to Worli. Free and traffic-free.

n: Eastern Express Highway ride to Thane
ad: Eastern Express Highway (start Sion/Matunga), Mumbai
d: Fast, wide highway stretch favoured by riders training for speed, often continued to the Yeoor Hills climb in Thane; finish with breakfast in Matunga.

ad: Start: Gorai Jetty, Borivali West, Mumbai 400091
d: Ferry across Gorai creek and ride the village roads, hills and beach of Gorai and Manori past the Global Vipassana Pagoda - an easy, roughly 22-30 km ride with a real out-of-city feel inside Mumbai.
t: Early morning (ferries from ~7 AM on organised rides)

n: Madh Island coastal ride: Madh jetty to Marve jetty
ad: Start: Madh jetty (Versova–Madh ferry), Madh, Mumbai
d: A city-only ride along Madh–Marve Road linking the island villages: Madh Fort and Madh Beach, then Erangal, Dana Pani, Aksa and on to Marve jetty. Riders can take the ferry across to Manori and continue on the Manori–Gorai road.

n: Marine Drive to Fort and Colaba loop
ad: Start: Marine Drive, near Girgaon Chowpatty, Mumbai 400020
d: A flat, roughly 15 km city ride: 3.5 km of seafront on Marine Drive, then Nariman Point, Churchgate, the Fort precinct and Colaba. Ride early morning or late night to avoid traffic.
t: Best early morning or late night

n: Mulund to Yeoor Hills MTB trail
ad: Start: Mulund West, Mumbai 400080
d: A hard (5/5) mountain-bike ride of about 12.7 km from Mulund into the Yeoor hills, with dirt sections, woods, lakes and monsoon waterfalls. Skilled riders only; don't ride solo.

ad: NCPA, Nariman Point, Mumbai (start/finish)
d: A 100 km loop around the city's edge — Western Express Highway, JVLR, Eastern Express Highway to Thane and back to NCPA — for riders chasing a century without leaving town.

n: Night ride: Colaba to Bandra (Regal to Mount Mary)
ad: Regal Cinema, Colaba, Mumbai (start)
d: A ~25 km night route past Gateway of India, Marine Drive, Worli Sea Face, Dadar Chowpatty and Bandstand to Mount Mary — the city at its emptiest.

n: Palm Beach Road ride (Vashi to Belapur)
ad: Palm Beach Road, starting Vashi, Navi Mumbai
d: Breezy, flat coastal road lined with palms, mangroves and lake views — a classic early-morning ride. Watch for fast traffic.

ad: Sewri Jetty / Sewri Fort, Sewri, Mumbai
d: Early-morning ride to the Sewri mudflats to see migrating flamingos in winter, with Sewri Fort overlooking the harbour.

n: SGNP: main gate to Kanheri Caves
ad: Sanjay Gandhi National Park main gate, Western Express Highway, Borivali East, Mumbai 400066
d: Mumbai's best-known forest ride: about 7 km one way on the park road, flat at first and then a steady climb to the Kanheri Caves. Cycles can be rented at the park entrance.

n: Uttan Road ride (Bhayandar West to Uttan)
ad: Start: Bhayandar (West) station area; end: Uttan Chowk / Uttan village
d: The road west from Bhayandar to the coast at Uttan runs past the villages of Rai, Murdha and Morva, with municipal lake gardens in several of them. A coastal road ride out of the city, best done early.

n: Western beaches ride: Uttan – Gorai – Manori – Marve – Aksa – Madh – Versova
ad: Start: Bhayander (Uttan road); city section from Gorai, Borivali West
d: A full-day, roughly 40 km coastal ride linking the western beaches, with two ferry hops (Manori to Marve, Madh jetty to Versova). Moderate.

ad: Start: Yeoor Hills gate, end of Pokhran Road 1, Thane West
d: The hill road into Yeoor, inside Sanjay Gandhi National Park, is Thane's nearest proper climb for cyclists: forest on both sides and little traffic early in the morning.

n: Andheri Sports Complex Pool (Shahaji Raje Krida Sankul)
ad: Andheri Sports Complex, Veera Desai Road, Andheri West, Mumbai 400053
d: BMC's sports complex with an Olympic-size pool and a four-level diving pool - the western suburbs' main competition-grade pool.

ad: Naupada, Thane West, Maharashtra 400602 (plus code 5XVC+3VJ)
d: Swimming pool in Naupada, central Thane West, for lap swimming and lessons.

ad: Dhokali, Thane West
d: Olympic-size public pool in the Dhokali-Balkum area, for serious laps or learn-to-swim batches.

n: BMC Andheri East Swimming Pool — Kondivita
ad: Kondivita Village, Andheri East, Mumbai
d: A BMC pool in Kondivita village, listed among the city pools running BMC's 21-day summer swimming courses.

n: BMC Andheri West Swimming Pool — Gilbert Hill
ad: Gilbert Hill, Andheri West, Mumbai
d: A BMC pool near Gilbert Hill, listed among the city pools running BMC's 21-day summer swimming courses.

n: BMC Dahisar Swimming Pool (Shri Mrubali Devi) — Kandarpada
ad: Kandarpada, Dahisar West, Mumbai 400068
d: A smaller BMC pool in Dahisar West, on annual membership via the BMC pool portal, and one of the venues for BMC's summer learn-to-swim camps.

n: BMC Malad Swimming Pool — Chacha Nehru Ground
ad: Chacha Nehru Ground, Malad West, Mumbai
d: A newer BMC pool at Chacha Nehru Ground, listed among the city pools running BMC's 21-day summer swimming courses.

ad: Mumbai

n: BMC Vikhroli Swimming Pool — Tagore Nagar
ad: Tagore Nagar, Vikhroli East, Mumbai
d: A BMC pool in Tagore Nagar, listed among the city pools running BMC's 21-day summer swimming courses.

n: BMC Wadala Swimming Pool — Wadala Fire Station
ad: Near Wadala Fire Station, Wadala, Mumbai
d: A BMC pool by the Wadala fire station, listed among the city pools running BMC's 21-day summer swimming courses.

n: BMC Worli Swimming Pool — Worli Reservoir Hill
ad: Worli Reservoir Hill, Worli, Mumbai
d: A BMC pool on Worli Reservoir Hill, listed among the city pools running BMC's 21-day summer swimming courses.

n: Bombay YMCA — Navi Mumbai Branch Swimming Pool
ad: YMCA Marg, Sector 8, CBD Belapur, Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra 400614
d: Swimming pool at the Bombay YMCA Navi Mumbai branch on YMCA Marg, CBD Belapur; the branch also has a gym and a basketball court.

ad: C'est La Vie, Hill Road, Bandra West, Mumbai 400050
d: A Bandra club with a year-round, temperature-controlled pool.

ad: 3256+6X8, Sector 9, Sanpada, Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra 400705
